newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's carmaker protests bankruptcy proposals.
newsitem.headline: Russia's carmaker protests bankruptcy proposals.

text.p: Top officials at Russia's biggest car maker AvtoVAZ protested on Wednesday against government proposals on Tuesday to start bankruptcy proceedings against the company, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Chairman Vladimir Kadannikov and chief executive Aleksei Nikolayev said in a statement they were ready for an open dialogue with the government but opposed strong-arm solutions.
"(Such solutions) will lead to the deterioration of a tough economic situation and will, in fact, dent the national industry," the statement said.
AvtoVAZ, which makes the Lada car, is Russia's eighth biggest company by sales, and with a workforce of 114,000, its fifth biggest employer, according to Ekspert magazine.

Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin called on Tuesday for the bankruptcy authorities to start proceedings against AvtoVAZ, which the government says is one of the country's biggest tax debtors.

Alfred Kokh, chairman of the State Property Commitee, Russia's privatisation ministry, said AvtoVAZ could choose between the official bankruptcy procedure and repaying its debts doubling its capital through a new share issued offered to new investors.
AvtoVAZ officials said these proposals contradicted earlier agreements with the government under which the company was given freedom to seek strategic investors to keep it in Russian hands.
The government says AvtoVAZ owes 2.8 trillion roubles ($508.3 million) in taxes. Officials said its total debt to the public sector and suppliers was 11 trillion roubles.
Kadannikov was Potanin's predecessor as first deputy premier in charge of the economy.
